cohort: 162 neonates from 1st day to 28 days of life, of either gender, or gestational age of <28 weeks presenting with neonatal sepsis were included.
finding: Staphylococcus aureus was the most frequent bacterial organism found in neonatal sepsis cases (44.4%), followed by Klebsiella (36.4%) and Escherichia Coli (29.6%), with common antibiotics showing varying sensitivity patterns.
cross-section timing: within the first 28 days of life
